question_to_decide: What is the current market price for each Week 10 game (spread, total, moneyline) and each player prop?
information_held_today: Nothing. Every market cell in every pack is blank by design and the official NFL site publishes no prices.
information_missing: A licensed sportsbook price feed or an official closing-line archive with timestamps.
current_answer: No price is known, so no edge, no CLV, no ROI and no leaderboard reward can be computed. Model lines are published as model expectations only.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Acquire a licensed feed, or capture closing lines manually under a written agreement; the NFL names Genius Sports as its exclusive data distribution partner for official play-by-play and Next Gen Stats.
blocks: every profitability claim, the leaderboard, CLV, the parlay pricing work

question_to_decide: What was the closing line for each bet so that closing-line value can be measured?
current_answer: CLV cannot be computed. It is the single strongest available luck control, because it compares the model with the market's final price rather than with a random outcome.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Subscribe to a closing-line archive, or record the closing screen weekly under a licence that permits research storage.
blocks: CLV gate, skill claims, leaderboard ordering

question_to_decide: How much of a strategy's apparent success is skill rather than luck?
information_held_today: A written protocol: training-only residuals, slate-clustered bootstrap intervals, Bonferroni correction across the frozen family, proper scoring rules, CLV.
information_missing: Enough out-of-sample observations to estimate the interval; no verified prices or results feed exists.
current_answer: Luck can be reduced but never eliminated. The honest statement today is that no strategy has enough out-of-sample data to separate skill from variance, and every published interval is blank because the inputs are blank.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Run the existing pipeline forward on a licensed feed for a full season, then report the interval width rather than a point estimate.

question_to_decide: Which historical games, scores and prices may be used as training data?
information_held_today: A trimmed 2015-2026 regular-season game log reconstructed from a community repository (PR #68, merged into this branch), whose sha256 was reproduced exactly from the upstream commit on 2026-11-13.
information_missing: A licence for the community dataset (the upstream repository declares no licence), and a first-party price source for the historical lines it contains.
current_answer: The dataset can be reconstructed byte-for-byte, so it is reproducible, but it carries no licence and its moneyline, spread and total columns are community-sourced rather than official. It is usable as a private prototype, not as a published first-party source.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Ask the upstream author for a licence, or replace the rows with a licensed feed before any published performance figure is relied on.

question_to_decide: Which player props exist, how are they settled and what is the base rate for each player-prop market?
information_held_today: A structural definition of the prop families to model and a settlement rule for each.
information_missing: An official prop catalogue, a settlement rule set and a historical sample of prop prices and outcomes.
current_answer: Nothing can be said about player-prop skill until prop markets and their outcomes can be observed. The official 2026 rulebook covers on-field rules, not sportsbook prop settlement.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Obtain the official sportsbook prop catalogue from the NFL's official partners and a licensed sample of prop outcomes.
blocks: the player-prop leg of the leaderboard

question_to_decide: What combinations may be offered as parlays, and what is the maximum number of legs and the pricing rule for each leg?
information_held_today: The mathematical machinery for joint probability and copula dependence is built and unit-tested in the repository.
information_missing: The official partner parlay rules, leg limits, and the price at which the book prices the joint event.
current_answer: Joint probability can be computed from marginals and a dependence structure, but without the bookmaker's own pricing rule the joint price cannot be priced the way the market prices it.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Request the written parlay rule set from an official partner; record it in the source register with the document identifier.

question_to_decide: When are injury statuses fixed, and what is the legal deadline after which a report cannot change?
information_held_today: The official Week 10 report structure: player, position, injuries, practice status and game status, republished continuously by the league.
information_missing: The written publication rule and deadline for each report type (the linked policy PDF did not return readable text in this session).
current_answer: Statuses can change up to the deadline, so an injury signal must be timestamped and frozen at a declared cut-off. Eighteen published practice-status claims differ from today's read, which is consistent with continuous republication rather than with error.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Read the official injury-report policy document and the CBA injury provisions, then freeze each week's capture at a declared timestamp.

question_to_decide: Which player is the 2nd, 3rd or 4th string at each position on each club, and how many snaps would the replacement take?
information_held_today: The structure: for every offensive and defensive position group, a 1st string starter, the depth order behind him, and a deficiency score.
information_missing: Official club depth charts for 29 clubs (only Washington, New York Giants and Detroit have one that was read) plus snap counts and play-level data.
current_answer: A deficiency score can only be computed when the official depth order and the replacement's expected snap share are known. Every published deficiency value is blank for that reason.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Collect the official depth chart page from each of the 32 clubs on a weekly basis with a capture timestamp, and pair it with a licensed snap-count feed.

question_to_decide: How many snaps does a replacement take and how much does that cost the unit?
information_held_today: Nothing official. The packs leave the EPA drop-off and the verified snap share blank.
information_missing: A licensed play-by-play feed with snap counts and an efficiency model.
current_answer: No depth or efficiency value can be published. The lines lab's structural severity index is an uncalibrated prior, not a measured effect.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Acquire a licensed play-by-play and efficiency feed, or keep every severity index labelled as a prior.
blocks: quantifying depth deficiency, the prop and single-bet sizing

question_to_decide: Who actually starts, as opposed to who is expected to start?
information_held_today: Official club announcements for a number of Week 10 positions (for example Cleveland's Deshaun Watson and Arizona's Carson Beck, both reported by NFL.com).
information_missing: A systematic official source that lists every club's starting lineup after the deadline.
current_answer: The individual announcements exist but there is no single official weekly lineup record. Starters can be confirmed from the NFL.com league roundups for the games in question.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Build a weekly capture of the NFL.com Friday roundup plus each club's official game-notes release, timestamped after the lineup deadline.

question_to_decide: How do trades, injuries and signings change a club's depth chart between the report and the game?
information_held_today: Several concrete examples read on 2026-11-13: Amani Hooker was acquired by Buffalo, Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates were traded out of Jacksonville, and Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve.
information_missing: A systematic transaction feed for all 32 clubs, tied to the weekly depth capture.
current_answer: Roster moves invalidate a depth chart captured earlier in the week. One published depth row still lists a Dallas player who had already moved to Buffalo before Week 10.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Capture the official NFL transaction page each week alongside the depth charts.

question_to_decide: Which wagers does the league itself consider objectionable, and does that constrain an injury-based strategy?
information_held_today: The league's own position, read directly: the three official partners agreed to prohibit wagers the league finds objectionable, including bets tied to officiating and injuries, and to prohibit wagers knowable in advance or easily manipulated by one person.
information_missing: Whether the league's policy extends to the intended use of an injury signal, and whether it is a contractual limit or only a statement of partner conduct.
current_answer: An injury-driven signal sits close to the line the league has drawn for its own partners. Any strategy whose value comes from knowing a starter is out is exposed to that policy and to the general NFL.com terms that prohibit systematic retrieval without written consent.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Ask the league or a partner in writing whether an injury-based research product is permitted; obtain qualified legal advice before publication.
blocks: the legality and the marketability of the injury strategy

question_to_decide: May this project collect official league data at all?
information_held_today: The NFL.com Terms and Conditions, read directly: use is limited to individual, non-commercial and informational purposes, and systematic retrieval that compiles a collection or database is prohibited without the league's express prior written consent.
information_missing: A written permission, or a licence for the data being used.
current_answer: The published pages link to official pages for citation. A general-purpose scraping or database build of league content would need written consent.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Request written consent from NFL Enterprises, or restrict the project to manual citation of official pages.
blocks: any automated collection of league data

question_to_decide: How many observations and how many slates are needed before a strategy can be qualified?
information_held_today: A written proposal: a minimum observation count and a minimum number of slate clusters, with Bonferroni correction across the frozen family of strategies.
information_missing: An agreed threshold that the owner accepts; the thresholds in the packs are proposals, not findings.
current_answer: The thresholds are design choices, not discovered facts. They should be fixed in writing before the first out-of-sample run, otherwise the qualification bar can be moved after seeing the result.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Owner decision recorded in the Suggestions register as decision S-01.

question_to_decide: What exactly is rewarded, and on which metric?
information_held_today: A design proposal: ranking on out-of-sample proper score and on closing-line value, with a qualifying threshold on both, and non-monetary recognition while no strategy qualifies.
information_missing: An owner decision on the reward and on the tie-break rule.
current_answer: No reward can be allocated today because no strategy qualifies. The reward rule should still be written down before any qualifying result appears, so that the rule cannot be tuned afterwards.
how_to_discover_the_missing_information: Owner decision recorded in the Suggestions register as decision S-02.
